cli-setup.title: Connect a development tool
cli-setup.intro: Configure and probe the tool on an execution node, then import its actual observations into this project. A template does not register a tool or execute a task.
cli-setup.entry: Absolute CLI entry path on the execution node
cli-setup.entry_help: Enter the installed .js, .mjs or .cjs entry path. It must exist on the execution node. The runner calls Node.js directly and checks the entry content digest, without a .cmd or shell launcher. Complete the absolute path to copy the configuration.
cli-setup.install: Install the selected CLI on the execution node and sign in through that tool.
cli-setup.configure: Save the template as a local command configuration and explicitly bind the project repository and full base commit.
cli-setup.observe: Run the read-only probe and inspect installation, version and protocol results. Missing or incompatible tools remain unavailable.
cli-setup.register: Import actual inventory, create and enable a tool profile, then preview a fixed dispatch plan from a task.
cli-setup.copy_failed: Copy did not complete. Select the configuration text and copy it manually.
cli-setup.harness_dependency: Harness also requires a compatible Multica runtime profile. The platform checks its versioned probe result and does not automatically install plugins or start a model.
cli-setup.codebuddy_policy: This template is for CodeBuddy Code. Its own permissions remain in force; pending authorization or unfinished background work prevents success. WorkBuddy is a separate product and needs its own service integration.
cli-setup.codex_policy: Codex uses a fixed workspace-write policy and an independent Git worktree for each development attempt.
cli-setup.probe_help: Replace REPOSITORY and COMMIT with the actual repository path and full commit. This command only produces probe observations.
cli-setup.shared_pool: Shared execution pools use the same local command allowlist from their pool configuration. Existing pool and project authorization and capacity checks still apply.
cli-setup.boundary: A successful help or protocol probe does not mean development is complete. Progress, code candidates, independent tests and explicit acceptance are stored separately.
cli-setup.planner_policy: Uses the locally built suma-agent.bundle.mjs with Node.js 22. Model and API address are fixed in the profile; API keys and the project-scoped Agent credential remain in the execution node environment. This does not create or validate a provider account.
cli-setup.planner_probe: The probe checks local installation and the planning protocol without calling the model. Import and enable its real observation in this project, then create a bounded analysis from Planning.
cli-setup.planner_entry_help: Enter the absolute suma-agent.bundle.mjs or .js entry on the execution node. The runner verifies the fixed entry content; a shell launcher is not used.
cli-setup.planner_install: Build or install the Suma native runtime and Node.js 22 on the execution node.
cli-setup.planner_configure: Save the local template, configure the fixed model and base URL, and supply API and project Agent credentials through that node’s environment.
cli-setup.planner_register: Import and enable the actual planning observation, then select it from the project Planning page.
